messages:
maria: Quick check — onboarding zeta-13b-v1. HF repo points to a redirecting origin: `hf://big-models/zeta/13b-v1` -> `s3://redwood-artifacts/prod/weights/zeta-13b-v1.tar.zst`. I kicked off a mirror but checksum failed on our side. Anyone run into HF->S3 redirect changing the digest/ETag?

tim: ETag != sha256 generally, S3 ETag can be multipart. If HF serves a presigned redirect the URL can include sig params but content should be identical. How are you computing checksum?

maria: Using `sha256sum` after download. Mirror job shows artifact-bot warning: `checksum mismatch` (see below). Downloaded file size matches. Not sure if decomposition changed during streaming.

artifact-bot: mirror job queued for repo big-models/zeta/13b-v1 -> s3://shadow-mirror/zeta/13b-v1.tar.zst

artifact-bot: mirror job completed with status: warning (checksum_mismatch). origin_etag: "d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e", local_sha256: "7f8c2e9..."

tim: Two quick things to validate: 1) Download with `--no-redirect` vs following redirects to confirm content. 2) Compare byte-level hashes: `curl -L "$URL" -o file && sha256sum file`. If HF serves a gzip-on-the-fly or changes meta it could alter bytes.

ashley: Also check tokenizer: last time we had a subtle failure when model weights came from a re-pack that changed tokenizers.json ordering. That created different special token ids (PAD=0 vs PAD=1) and caused model to misalign during embedding lookup. Might explain a mismatch only seen at runtime, not purely checksum.

kevin: For registry validation: make sure manifest includes both origins and explicit checksum fields. Example manifest snippet we validate against: ```json
{"model": "zeta-13b-v1", "origins": {"hf": "hf://big-models/zeta/13b-v1", "s3": "s3://redwood-artifacts/prod/weights/zeta-13b-v1.tar.zst"}, "checksum_sha256": "<hex>", "tokenizer_version": "2025-09-01"}
```

maria: Thanks — I re-downloaded with `curl -L` and got same sha256 as mirror file, so bytes match our mirror. HF origin shows an http 302 to a presigned s3 URL; maybe HF returns a zero-length ETag header or a placeholder. How do we want to surface this to users?

tim: We should normalize on content-hash (sha256) for all registry entries. ETag can be stored as metadata but not trusted for validation. Also add a small md5 header check for quick sanity.

ashley: Re tokenizer: I pulled tokenizer.json from both sources and diffed them. The token index for "<pad>" is different. Quick patch suggestion: our loader should assert canonical special token ids match the manifest's `tokenizer_specials` map and fail fast with clear error.

maria: Ok plan: 1) Update manifest to include `checksum_sha256` and `tokenizer_specials` mapping. 2) Re-run mirror (force-download) and set artifact-bot to revalidate. 3) If checksum still mismatches, escalate to HF support.

artifact-bot: mirror job queued (force=true) for big-models/zeta/13b-v1 -> s3://shadow-mirror/zeta/13b-v1.tar.zst

kevin: Also add a small CI gate that runs `python -c "import json,sys; m=json.load(open('manifest.json')); assert 'checksum_sha256' in m"` so PRs can't land without the checksum.

maria: I'll push a manifest patch and tag you all. If anyone can review fast — mostly just adding two fields. Thanks! :pray:

tim: Ping me when ready, I'll sanity-check the presigned headers and multipart flags. :thumbsup:

ashley: I'll run tokenizer diff after you push. If it needs remapping we can add a migration step to the onboarding pipeline.
